statement:
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a category.
The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item Nonempty finite limits exist in $\mathcal{C}$.
\item Products of pairs and equalizers exist in $\mathcal{C}$.
\item Products of pairs and fibre products exist in $\mathcal{C}$.
\end{enumerate}
semantic_review_note: Independently checked categories.tex lines 2022–2029 and surrounding finite-limit conventions: existence of ALL finite NONEMPTY limits in C, existence of pair products and equalizers, and existence of pair products and fibre products are THREE EQUIVALENT conditions. No final-object condition is inserted into this nonempty variant.

statement:
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a category.
The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item Finite limits exist in $\mathcal{C}$.
\item Finite products and equalizers exist.
\item The category has a final object and fibre products exist.
\end{enumerate}
semantic_review_note: Source lemma at lines 2047–2054 has three-way equivalence for ALL finite limits (including empty diagram): finite limits; finite products with equalizers; final object with fibre products. Reviewed final content retains terminal-object condition and all three clauses; it is not the weaker nonempty finite-limit statement from the preceding lemma.
